root.label: Access control and friends
root.note: Access is a permission on names, checked after lookup and overload resolution.

children.label: Checked last
children.note: Lookup and overload resolution ignore access; the chosen name is then checked.

children.label: Private best match
children.note: A private overload that wins resolution makes the call ill-formed, not redirected.

children.label: Private still hides
children.note: A private base member hides a global of the same name; qualify with ::.

children.label: Names, not types
children.note: auto can hold a private nested type because the private name is never spelled.

children.label: Virtual calls
children.note: Access is checked on the static type's function; a private override still runs.

children.label: Protected rule
children.note: Protected non-static members are reachable only through the accessing class or its derived classes.

children.label: Not through Base&
children.note: Derived may not read a protected member through a plain Base reference.

children.label: Pointer to member
children.note: Must be formed as &Derived::m, which still has type T Base::*.

children.label: Static members exempt
children.note: The extra check applies only to non-static members.

children.label: Friends
children.note: A friend gets the same access as the granting class's own members.

children.label: Kinds
children.note: Functions, member functions, classes, and class or function templates can be friends.

children.label: Not inherited
children.note: A class derived from a friend gets no access.

children.label: Not transitive
children.note: A friend of a friend gets nothing, and friendship is not reciprocal.

children.label: Hidden friends
children.note: Defined in the class, found only by ADL, so they stay out of unrelated overload sets.

children.label: Base access
children.note: Inheritance access caps the access of inherited members and controls conversion to the base.

children.label: Defaults
children.note: class inherits privately and struct publicly; members default the same way.

children.label: Derived-to-base
children.note: Converting to a private base outside the class and its friends is ill-formed.

children.label: using-declaration
children.note: Can make an accessible inherited member public, protected or private in the derived class.

children.label: Injected-class-name
children.note: Inherited through a private base, the plain class name becomes inaccessible; use ::A.

children.label: Templates
children.note: Access checks interact with substitution and with explicit instantiation.

children.label: SFINAE
children.note: Since C++11 access is checked during substitution, so a private member reads as absent.

children.label: Explicit instantiation
children.note: Names in its declaration skip access checks, so a private member can be a template argument.

children.label: Nested and local
children.note: Classes inside classes and functions inherit the access of their surroundings.

children.label: Nested class
children.note: A member of the enclosing class, so it may use all its private names (C++11).

children.label: One-way only
children.note: The enclosing class has no special access to the nested class's private members.

children.label: Local class
children.note: May use the names its enclosing function may use, including that class's private members.
